sourceFacts: One cast-iron tensile chart, origin 0, upward stress axis sigma with multiplier x10^5 N/m^2, rightward strain epsilon axis in percent.
Six stress labels ascend 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000, 1200 with approximately equal vertical intervals.
The only numbered nonzero strain labels are decimal-comma 0,1 and 0,5. Their approximate physical readings are 0.1 percent and 0.5 percent; retain the printed comma labels visibly.
A thick solid concave-down increasing curve starts at the origin and ends at the 1200 guide. It is not a straight line and has no plateau or invented continuation.

Four solid horizontal guides are visible at 600, 800, 1000 and 1200. The 600 guide is very short because the curve is close to the stress axis there. Do not add full-width 200/400 guides or a full rectangular grid.

Three solid vertical projections descend from the 800, 1000 and 1200 curve intersections. The 800 projection is associated with the 0,1 label; the 1000 foot is unnumbered; the terminal projection is near the 0,5 label.
There is no distinct long 600 vertical projection. Source stroke overlap near the origin is not evidence for a new grid column.
No labelled data points, fracture marker, 0.45 tick, erratum, dashed curve, or quantitative values beyond the printed scales are drawn.
The source caption is Figure 89, outside the crop. This figure belongs to n52, not the following n53 heading.
